hypotheses.confidence_note: Conditional two-second local prototype, not verified world safety. Revision 1 repairs PREMISE_SPACE by making the finite actor-accounting scope contain every retained whole-body source, including the oncoming sedan initially extending to x=31.5 and the left wagon extending to y=12.4. The drivable road polygon, target region, actor positions, motion alternatives, residuals and safety requirements are unchanged. The scope rectangle is not additional drivable pavement: only road.polygon_m defines the modeled continuous pavement. Geometry and residuals remain uncalibrated visual hypotheses. Ego initially travels at 8.818 m/s; the 7 m/s preference requires physically limited deceleration. A modest rightward displacement may be necessary for oncoming clearance and requires independent full-body feasibility checking. No optimizer, independent collision check or prefix simulation has been executed here. Sidewalk pedestrians and rear traffic are conditionally excluded from entering the modeled driving interior; the forward white lead car and distant traffic are conditionally assumed to remain beyond the finite scene's forward boundary. The left SUV, silver wagon and oncoming sedan remain explicit obstacles.

premises.statement: For these two seconds the finite local scene domain is x in [-4,33] m and y in [-6.5,13.5] m. It contains the unchanged modeled road patch, the observed left entrance and the complete body envelopes of all five retained actors, with room for their declared total residuals. This is an actor-accounting domain, not a claim that its entire rectangle is drivable: permitted pavement remains exactly road.polygon_m, and permitted ego centers remain target_region. Its forward and lateral extent is set by the already estimated oncoming sedan body and left entrance wagon body, not by solver feasibility. Adopt no additional unobserved entrant into this domain during the horizon. Observed sidewalk pedestrians, including the right-side man and rear-right group, remain outside the modeled paved driving interior; no pedestrian curb entry, door opening or rear-traffic incursion occurs. The forward white lead car and more distant forward traffic remain wholly beyond x=33 m without moving backward into this domain. These are falsifiable local exclusions rather than claims about an empty world. The declared oncoming sedan remains fully modeled throughout its approach; the left SUV and wagon obey their separate waiting or creeping conditions. All retained actor source polygons are contained in this scope.

Approximate metric reconstruction assumes the stated ordinary passenger-vehicle body dimensions, approximately level local pavement, and visible curb and vehicle perspective consistent with supplied camera axes. Individual dimensions and visual center/depth estimates are conditional priors. Road edges are estimated from curb convergence in the reference front and near-reference side images; the local pavement polygon uses those directions with a separate 0.4 m residual. Calibration supplies orientation and camera origin, not certified depth. This unrestricted spatial premise supports the cited metric estimates, including the asynchronous observation.

The broadside black SUV at the left entrance is conditionally waiting. Adopt fixed center and heading; the adverse variant creeps toward negative y at 0 to 0.2 m/s, total displacement at most 0.4 m, with heading fixed and x displacement at most 0.1 m. Sustained entry or acceleration into the ego lane is excluded by this explicit short-term hypothesis. Its broadside position across the supplied front history supports waiting but does not guarantee it. The supplied rectangles enclose the entire body under both retained conditions for the whole interval.

The oncoming sedan travels toward negative x. Adopt speed 4 to 7 m/s and center y within 3.55 to 3.65 m; the reasonable adverse variant permits speed 0 to 9 m/s and center y within 3.4 to 3.8 m. Body yaw remains within 0.02 rad of pi. These conditions are consistent with an approaching vehicle remaining on its side of the road but are not measured future guarantees. The whole-interval rectangles enclose all body positions and permitted yaw spread, including the native initial body at x=29 m. No forecast is delegated to tools.

These curbside sedans remain parked for two seconds without opening doors. Adopt fixed native body poses. Adverse pose-spread alternatives allow center perturbation up to 0.05 m per axis and yaw perturbation up to 0.02 rad, still stationary. The supplied rectangles include those full-body perturbations. Pulling out is excluded by this conditional hypothesis.

The dark curbside sedan is individually observed in CAM_FRONT_LEFT 0.007605 s before reference. Its evidence position is estimated in fixed reference axes using the supplied capture ego pose and camera orientation. Across this actual past age, assume ground speed no greater than 0.2 m/s, giving displacement at most 0.001521 m, rounded outward to 0.002 m for both retained scenarios. Its parked appearance supports this conditional bound; a 0.2 m alignment residual additionally covers visual registration. Future stationary conditions and adverse static pose spread are separately declared. This premise covers the actual evidence-to-reference interval as well as the future horizon.

The silver wagon at the far-left entrance remains waiting, or creeps toward negative y at no more than 0.25 m/s for two seconds. Its heading is fixed at the native broadside estimate and x displacement is at most 0.1 m. Faster entry or turning across the road is excluded conditionally. Its complete body is retained in both whole-interval source polygons, not clipped to the drivable road patch.

anchors.rationale: The individually visible broadside black crossover/SUV is assigned an ordinary midsize-SUV length prior matching its native body geometry.
The individually visible silver sedan rear is assigned a passenger-sedan width prior matching its native body geometry.

metric_scale_support.metric_reasoning: The black SUV spans roughly a few hundred horizontal pixels broadside in the reference front image; a 4.8 m length prior and approximately 1253 px focal length imply a depth on the order of twenty metres after accounting for transverse pose. The right parked sedan's rear width and ground-contact perspective independently suggest a low-twenties-metre body center. Camera-axis rays give approximate lateral offsets. These anchors, the visible yellow center lines, parking markings and curb convergence support the proposed local dimensions and curb directions. The road polygon is unchanged in this repair: its near and far lateral boundaries follow the estimated visible curb directions, while its longitudinal truncation covers the current footprint and intended two-second route. The larger premise domain only contains already-declared actor bodies and is not used as a pavement estimate. Ground contact and level-pavement assumptions remain approximate; no certified ground-plane calibration or exact pixel fit is claimed.
